metadata.title: Tesla Cash Burn Puts AI Spending in Focus

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Tesla (TSLA, Financials), the electric vehicle and energy company, is expected to report its first quarterly cash burn in more than two years as expenditure on artificial intelligence, robotics and manufacturing rises sharply. LSEG figures show Wall Street estimates free cash flow to drop to negative $3.3 billion in the second quarter.Tesla will invest around $25 billion on data centers, AI infrastructure and production capacity this year. The scale of expenditure is a test of whether the company's core car and energy businesses can afford its bigger ambitions.What investors are laser-focused on are Robotaxis, Full Self-Driving and the Optimus humanoid robot. Progress has been slower than many had hoped and a number of growth targets have been delayedTesla's robotaxi service is still limited to a handful of U.S. locations. The company is already making the Cybercab, but not yet rolling it out more widely.The auto industry is starting to revive. Tesla recorded record sales for the second quarter, and experts are forecasting a 3.9% gain in full-year volume to 1.7 million vehicles.However margins are still under pressure. Automotive gross margin, excluding regulatory credits, is expected to dip to 18.1% by Wall Street.Attention now turns to Wednesday's earnings call, when investors will be looking for signs that Tesla's AI investing is starting to pay off commercially.
